title: openai-compat: adaptive tool aliasing and choice-priority resolver
author: Sofia Chen
description: Context: We're seeing subtle differences in tool selection when downstream systems expect tool aliases (e.g., 'weather' vs 'weather_v2') and when model-produced tool_choice signals arrive as ranked lists or soft-probabilities. This PR introduces an adaptive aliasing layer plus a priority-resolver that normalizes tool_choice semantics across streaming and non-streaming paths.
summary: Adds a canonical alias map, selection weighting resolver, and streaming-safe tool-choice handling to the OpenAI compatibility adapter. Preserves backwards compatibility while enabling deterministic fallbacks and tunable preference weights for enterprise tool routing.
motivation_and_rationale: Operators previously had to maintain brittle 1:1 name mappings in the application layer. With multiple model variants and function name drift, misrouted tool invocations caused retries and incorrect outputs. This change centralizes alias resolution and introduces a priority resolver that consumes: 1) explicit tool_choice entries, 2) streaming partial tool hints, and 3) operator-provided preference weights to produce a single canonical tool invocation decision.
design_highlights:
- alias_map: YAML-backed mapping supporting exact, prefix, and regex aliases with optional deprecation metadata.
- priority_resolver: scoring pipeline that combines operator weight, model confidence (soft or hard), and recent invocation success metrics.
- streaming_adapter: incremental aggregation of partial tool_choice fragments to avoid premature invocations while maintaining low latency.
- compatibility_mode: feature flag to toggle strict legacy 1:1 resolution for customers that rely on old semantics.
api_changes:
- New optional parameter in /v1/compat/dispatch: 'alias_profile' (string) and 'choice_resolution' (enum: strict|adaptive|legacy).
- SDK: redwood-sdk-python adds DispatchOptions.alias_profile and .choice_resolution with docs and example.
- Admin: YAML schema for alias_map under /config/openai/aliases.yaml.
Note: Default remains legacy-compatible but uses adaptive resolution for new accounts.
rollout_plan:
1) feature gated behind 'openai_adaptive_aliasing' runtime flag; 2) start with internal canary (10% traffic) for 48h; 3) enable for PLG accounts opted-in; 4) full rollout after two weeks if no regressions.
Traffic routing includes automatic fallback to the previous resolver when invocation error rate increases above 2x baseline.
migration_notes: Operators can supply an alias_profile to map existing tooling names. A migration tool (scripts/migrate_aliases.py) is included to convert customer-provided CSVs into the YAML alias_map format. Backwards compatibility tests included for customers with strict mappings.

review_conversation: Evelyn Park (reviewer): Can you clarify how regex aliases interact with prefix aliases when both match? Suggested deterministic tie-break: longest literal match wins.
Sofia Chen (author): Implemented longest-literal first, then regex ordering by specificity. Added test 'test_regex_vs_prefix_ordering'.
Rahul Iyer (reviewer): Concern about the 120ms buffer in streaming_adapter on high-throughput stable customers. Can we make this adaptive?
Sofia Chen (author): Switched to an adaptive hold window (min 20ms, max 200ms) and added heuristics based on recent token latency. Documented in aliasing.md.
Tomás Alvarez (approver): Verified canary metrics: no change in 95th p50 latency, error rate decreased for aliases with multiple names. Approving.
